heroHeadline: Day 604: Mexico Expels Two CIA Agents in Sovereignty Action; USMCA Round 1 Opens in Mexico City (Ebrard-Goettman); Sheinbaum Publishes Asset Declaration; CNTE Dialogue Ahead of June 1 Mega-March
heroSubtitle: May 28, 2026 marks Day 604 of Claudia Sheinbaum's presidency — a day of simultaneous confrontation and cooperation with Washington. At her morning mañanera, Sheinbaum confirmed Mexico expelled two surviving CIA agents who participated without proper accreditation in the April 19, 2026 Chihuahua anti-drug operation — Mexico's most concrete sovereignty enforcement action against the United States under her presidency. The agents entered legally but failed to register intelligence activities; Mexico issued a diplomatic note and they complied. Simultaneously, USMCA Round 1 formally opened at Mexico's Ministry of Economy in Mexico City, with Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard leading Mexico's delegation and Deputy USTR Jeff Goettman leading the U.S. side (USTR Greer attended by video after being recalled by Trump on May 27). Round 1 agenda: rules of origin, Chinese nearshoring restrictions, and economic security framework. Ebrard acknowledged publicly that a clean 16-year extension by the July 1 USMCA deadline is unlikely; a provisional agreement with continued talks is more probable. Round 2 is June 16–17 in Washington; Round 3 the week of July 20 in Mexico City. Also on Day 604: Sheinbaum's 2026 asset declaration was published — annual income of 1.79 million pesos (presidential salary) and an 8% stake in two family manufacturing companies. Security Secretary García Harfuch explained why Rocha Moya was not detained despite his FGR appearance and Interpol red notice — the FGR had not yet filed for pretrial detention. Interior Secretary Rodríguez confirmed a second SEGOB-CNTE dialogue session ahead of the union's threatened June 1 mega-march toward the Zócalo during the FIFA World Cup opening weekend. Sheinbaum also confirmed she will give away her presidential inauguration match ticket through a contest for young women who love soccer.
